trickyParts: assistant-ui applies a rebuilt transcript in a passive effect, one commit after the render carrying the new ids, so a layout effect that compensates immediately measures the old DOM and moves the reader by nothing. The hook holds a rebuild and settles it in the commit the turns change in, watched with a MutationObserver that is connected only in that window.

Chromium's scroll anchoring answers a shorter rebuild by subtracting the dropped height a frame later. That arrives at the scroll listener as a fall in scrollTop with the new height already recorded, which read as the reader scrolling and undid the jump to the live end. The hook excuses exactly the one event whose scrollHeight equals the height its settle recorded.

assistant-ui's own scroll-up detector requires scrollHeight to be unchanged, so it never notices a reader scrolling back while a turn streams - this issue's own case - and its follow flag is internal. That is why all four of its auto-scroll options are off rather than scrollToBottomOnRunStart alone.

A turn shown as a streamed frame and the same turn shown as its stored Dispatch copy must be one turn across a rebuild, so both carry the key dispatch:<id>; the merged list and the DOM attribute derive it from one helper.

Nothing in the suite could make an already-connected live view take a second replay: ?as=replay only sets what the next connection is answered with, and Chromium's offline emulation does not end the agent stream's in-flight fetch (measured: the view stayed Live for 15s while the shell's own pill flipped). Hence the ?as=drop test hook, modelled on /api/v1/events/_test/disconnect.
deviations: The plan's D4 (an unconditional jump to the newest text on every rebuild, with acceptance line A8) was replaced mid-phase by the architect with spec v9's rule, which Sami chose: keep the reader's place when the rebuilt transcript still carries the turn they were reading, the newest text otherwise. A8 is therefore two rows rather than one, and the rebuild compensates the remembered turn's offset rather than holding scrollTop.

The plan's A11 asserted an unchanged threadScrollTop when a folded tool call is expanded. A fold opened in the middle of the screen moves scrollTop by its own height through the browser's own scroll anchoring, which is what holds the reader still, so the row asserts the reader's turn and its offset instead - the thing the spec says must not move.
The plan did not foresee a server change. The ?as=drop test hook (gated by DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS, as every other _test route is) was the only way to reach the rebuild path from a browser.
discoveredComplexity: The pod was replaced twice during this phase, taking /tmp and ~/.cache with it. The harness now lives on the issue volume (/legion/harness/setup.sh, env.sh: the Postgres build and data, the Playwright browsers, GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE), which is roughly 1.2G of scratch moved off the container filesystem - evidence for dispatch://INFRA-31's ephemeral-storage hypothesis, reported to the architect. The tester inherits that harness; re-run setup.sh, which is idempotent, and never stop a sibling's Postgres.
